stem: By which amendment was the voting age reduced from 21 to 18 in India?
subject: Polity
explanation: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 reduced the minimum voting age from 21 to 18 years for elections to Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.

stem: The 42nd Amendment (1976) is called the 'Mini Constitution' because it:

options.is_correct: Made sweeping changes — added Fundamental Duties, changed Preamble, extended Emergency provisions, amended many articles

subject: Polity
explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) was the most wide-ranging, adding 'socialist' and 'secular' to the Preamble, inserting Fundamental Duties (Art. 51A), and making far-reaching changes to governance structure.

stem: Which amendment added 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
subject: Polity
explanation: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment, 1976 (during Emergency) inserted 'Socialist' and 'Secular' before 'Democratic Republic' in the Preamble and 'Unity and Integrity' in place of 'Unity'.

stem: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992) is significant for:

options.is_correct: Constitutionally recognising Panchayati Raj institutions and adding Part IX to the Constitution

subject: Polity
explanation: The 73rd Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions and added Part IX (Articles 243–243O) and the 11th Schedule (29 functions).

options.is_correct: Urban local bodies — Municipalities (added Part IX-A and 12th Schedule)

subject: Polity
explanation: The 74th Amendment added Part IX-A to the Constitution dealing with Municipalities (Nagarpalikas), added the 12th Schedule (18 functions), and constitutionalised urban local self-governance.

stem: Which amendment introduced the Anti-Defection Law (10th Schedule)?
subject: Polity
explanation: The 52nd Constitutional Amendment, 1985 introduced the Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law), disqualifying members of Parliament/State Legislature who defect from their parties.

stem: The 44th Amendment (1978) reversed many changes made by the 42nd Amendment. It notably deleted which Fundamental Right?

options.is_correct: Right to Property (Article 31) — making it a legal right under Article 300A

subject: Polity
explanation: The 44th Amendment, 1978 removed the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights (it had been Article 19(1)(f) and 31) and made it a constitutional right under Article 300A.

stem: The 86th Amendment (2002) made which right a Fundamental Right?

options.is_correct: Right to free and compulsory education for children aged 6–14 (Article 21-A)

subject: Polity
explanation: The 86th Amendment inserted Article 21-A, making free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for children between 6 and 14 years. It also amended Articles 45 and 51A(k).

options.is_correct: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — inserting Article 246A and the GST Council

subject: Polity
explanation: The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 enabled the introduction of GST by inserting Article 246A (GST), Article 269A (IGST), and establishing the GST Council under Article 279A.

options.is_correct: 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) in education and public employment

options.option_text: Extension of reservation for 10 more years

subject: Polity
explanation: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment, 2019 added Articles 15(6) and 16(6) to provide up to 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections not covered under existing reservation categories.

stem: The 24th Amendment (1971) overturned which Supreme Court ruling by asserting Parliament's power to amend any part of the Constitution?
subject: Polity
explanation: In the Golaknath case (1967) the Supreme Court held that Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights. The 24th Amendment (1971) overturned this by affirming Parliament's unlimited amending power.

stem: By which amendment was the National Commission for Scheduled Castes and National Commission for Scheduled Tribes separated?
subject: Polity
explanation: The 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 bifurcated the earlier combined National Commission for SCs and STs into two separate commissions — NCSC and NCST.

stem: The procedure to amend the Indian Constitution is laid down in:
subject: Polity
explanation: Article 368 lays down the procedure for amendment of the Constitution. It provides for three methods: simple majority, special majority, and special majority + ratification by at least half the states.

stem: The 97th Amendment (2011) added provisions relating to:

options.is_correct: Co-operative Societies — inserting Article 19(1)(c) protection and Part IX-B

subject: Polity
explanation: The 97th Constitutional Amendment gave constitutional status to co-operative societies, inserting Article 43-B and Part IX-B, guaranteeing the right to form cooperative societies.

stem: Which amendment extended reservation for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies for 10 more years up to 2030?
subject: Polity
explanation: The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 extended the reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies for a further 10 years (to 25 January 2030) and ended Anglo-Indian nominated seats.

stem: The 25th Amendment (1971) curtailed the right to compensation for property acquired by the State. It replaced the word 'compensation' with:

options.is_correct: 'Amount' (removing the right to adequate compensation — Article 31(2))

subject: Polity
explanation: The 25th Amendment replaced 'compensation' with 'amount' in Article 31(2), effectively removing the right to receive full market-value compensation for compulsory acquisition.

stem: Which constitutional amendment restored the primacy of the Directive Principles over some Fundamental Rights (overturning Kesavananda Bharati judgment in part)?

options.is_correct: 42nd Amendment (1976) — Article 31-C expanded to cover all DPSPs

subject: Polity
explanation: The 42nd Amendment expanded Article 31-C to cover all Directive Principles, giving them precedence over Articles 14, 19, and 31 — partly reversed later by the Minerva Mills case (1980).

stem: The Right to Education Act (RTE) was implemented under which constitutional amendment?
subject: Polity
explanation: The 86th Amendment inserted Article 21A (Right to Education). The RTE Act, 2009 was the legislation passed to give effect to this constitutional provision.
